summary: This informational RFC moves several outdated TCP extensions and related documents to Historic status because they were superseded, never widely used, or are no longer recommended. The affected documents are RFCs 675, 721, 761, 813, 816, 879, 896, 1078 and 6013. It updates RFC 7414.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7805 updates the status labels for older TCP documents. It marks some as Historic because they were superseded or should no longer be used, and marks others Informational because they remain useful as background or advice.

subtitle: A status update for TCP documents that had been superseded, little used, or no longer recommended.

tldr.problem: The TCP roadmap described old documents as Historic or Informational, but their status in the RFC database had not been changed accordingly.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7805 reclassifies nine RFCs as Historic and eight as Informational, giving a short reason for each change.
tldr.outcome: The memo makes the status changes identified in the TCP roadmap and updates RFC 7414. RFC 7805 itself is Informational.

today: RFC 7805 is Informational and updates RFC 7414. It reclassifies the older TCP documents listed in its status-change sections.

sections.title: Why the Status Changes Were Needed
sections.content:
Many RFCs describe TCP, its implementation, and its extensions. Some were superseded, some were no longer recommended, and some had not seen widespread use. The TCP roadmap, RFC 7414, had already discussed status changes, but it did not ask the RFC Editor to update the RFC database.

RFC 7805 carries out those status changes. It also classifies other TCP-related documents with Unknown status as either Historic or Informational.
sections.plainLanguage: The TCP roadmap identified old documents that needed different status labels. This RFC updates the labels in the RFC record.

sections.title: Documents Moved to Historic
sections.content:
Nine RFCs are moved to Historic. RFCs 675 and 761 were replaced by RFC 793, while RFC 721 proposed control signals that were not included in RFC 793. RFCs 813, 816, 879, and 896 had material incorporated into later documents named by this memo.

The RFC also says TCPMUX (RFC 1078) should be deprecated because it changes connection-establishment behavior, puts new connections on one port, complicates firewall management, and had very limited reported deployment. TCP Cookie Transactions (RFC 6013) is also moved to Historic because it uses experimental TCP option codepoints and had no known wide-scale deployment.
sections.plainLanguage: The Historic group includes old TCP specifications replaced by newer documents and proposals that were not adopted. The memo also moves TCPMUX and TCP Cookie Transactions because it says they should be deprecated.

sections.title: Documents Moved to Informational
sections.content:
Eight RFCs are moved from Unknown to Informational. The memo keeps them available as reports, background, implementation suggestions, experiments, or technical observations rather than treating them as current protocol rules.

The group includes an early TCP deployment report, guidance on resource management and identifier tables, implementation suggestions, a discussion of TCP on local networks, retransmission-timeout experiments, a critique of a military TCP specification, and techniques for computing the Internet checksum.
sections.plainLanguage: The Informational group contains older reports and advice that can still help readers understand TCP history or implementation. Their new label does not present them as current standards.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 7805 introduces no new security considerations. It says that each listed RFC attempts to address security considerations for the specification or subject it contains.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC changes document status labels and introduces no new security considerations.
